match.reason: The bank point is written for Year 11 Victorian Economics and adds cost-benefit analysis and trade-off ideas beyond the Year 7 point, so changing it would mean a change of depth rather than small edits.

draft.title: Opportunity cost
card: Because of scarcity, people must choose. Choosing one thing means giving up others.
Opportunity cost is the next best choice you give up when you make a decision.
It is only the next best choice, not every choice given up. If you spend the afternoon riding your bike, and swimming was your second pick, the swim is the opportunity cost.
Opportunity cost is not always money. It can be time, effort or any other benefit you miss out on.
draft.remember: Opportunity cost is what you give up: the next best choice.

a.q: Jack has a free afternoon. He ranks his options: 1 football, 2 reading, 3 video games. He chooses football. What is his opportunity cost?
opts: The money he spent on football boots
a.why: Opportunity cost is the next best choice given up, which is Jack's second pick, reading. Video games are also given up, but they are not the next best option.
a.clue: Which choice came second on his list?

b.q: Mei's family has a spare block of land in Tasmania. They can grow potatoes, graze sheep or build a shed. They rank them in that order and choose potatoes. What is the opportunity cost?
opts: Building a shed on the land
Grazing sheep and building a shed
The seeds needed to plant the potatoes
b.why: The family gives up the next best use of the land, which is grazing sheep. The shed is also given up, but it was ranked last, so it is not the opportunity cost.
b.clue: Find the option ranked just below the one chosen.

problems.detail: The clue 'Which choice came second on his list?' gives the answer away. A student can pick 'Reading' by reading the list without knowing that opportunity cost is the next best choice.
The clue 'Find the option ranked just below the one chosen' points straight to grazing sheep. It turns the question into a list lookup rather than a test of the idea.
